candidates.title: Montréal to Rivière-du-Loup on Route 20
candidates.summary: The south-shore drive that starts the loop, with room for frequent stops for the seven-year-old. Drive time is unmeasured, and the access needs were not answered, so the stops should be planned around those needs.

candidates.title: Rivière-du-Loup to Saint-Siméon by ferry
candidates.summary: A short crossing that breaks up the drive and gets the car onto the north shore, which the party has already driven. Ferry schedules and seasonal operation were not checked, so confirm them before relying on this.

candidates.title: Sainte-Flavie to Percé via Route 132
candidates.summary: The coastal drive along the Gaspé shore toward Percé Rock, one of the stops the party already wants. Frequent pull-offs suit the seven-year-old, though drive time and fuel are estimates only.

candidates.title: Percé to Forillon National Park by Route 132
candidates.summary: A coastal leg from Percé to the Forillon area, the park the party already wants to see. Campground showers at Forillon were not checked against the one-night limit.

candidates.title: Forillon back to Sainte-Flavie via Gaspé
candidates.summary: The return up the north side of the peninsula, closing the loop toward Rivière-du-Loup. Durations and campground showers along the way were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A basic guesthouse kind of place near Forillon gives a simple night close to the park stop. Access needs were not answered, so accessibility is unknown to me. Season and booking lead time were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple cabin kind of place with a private shower avoids the one-night limit on campgrounds without showers. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot confirm accessibility. Season and booking lead time were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Percé Rock and Bonaventure Island boat trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: The rock and its seabird colony are the reason many people come to the Gaspé, and a boat trip to Bonaventure Island shows gannets up close. I have not checked current departure times, so timing and whether the trip suits a seven-year-old are unknown to me. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot judge boarding or walking on the island.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park coastal walks
candidatesAccepted.summary: Forillon offers short coastal trails and cliff viewpoints that can be stopped and started, which suits a child who tires in the car. I have not confirmed trail lengths or current park fees. Access needs were not answered, so trail suitability is unknown.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cap-des-Rosiers lighthouse stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short roadside stop at a working lighthouse on the Forillon coast, a good break point on the drive. I have not checked opening hours or whether the site is open in July, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bakery stop in Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A morning bread and pastry stop before the Percé Rock walk, good for a short break that suits the seven-year-old. I could not account for access needs, since that was not answered, so check any requirements before choosing this stop.

candidatesAccepted.title: Wharf seafood takeout in Gaspé
candidatesAccepted.summary: Fresh fish and shellfish eaten by the harbour makes an easy lunch between stops and needs no reservation. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot confirm seating or step-free access.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A casual seaside lunch that suits a family wanting to stop often rather than push through. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot say whether the seating is accessible.

candidatesAccepted.title: Picnic lunch at Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: Bring provisions from a town grocery and eat at a park picnic area, which keeps costs low and gives the children room to move. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot confirm the picnic area's accessibility.

candidatesAccepted.title: Roadside treat stop in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A quick stop for local baked goods or preserves, useful for breaking up the drive for children. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot account for them here.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ice cream stop in Sainte-Anne-des-Monts
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short treat stop on the coast road that helps the seven-year-old through a long stretch of driving. Access needs were not answered, so I cannot say whether the shop is step-free.

candidatesAccepted.title: Percé Rock waterfront stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short, easy stop at the rock the family already wants, with room to stretch and break up the drive. I could not account for access needs, which were not answered, so check accessibility on arrival. Duration and season were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park coastal visit
candidatesAccepted.summary: A park stop the family already wants, with coastline and trails that suit the moderate effort level and frequent breaks. Access needs were not answered, so I could not account for them. Park fees and season were not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bonaventure Island seabird boat trip
candidatesAccepted.summary: A boat outing to a seabird colony, a different experience from the north shore they have already done. Boat schedules and whether a seven-year-old will tolerate the crossing are unknown to me, and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Miguasha fossil park visit
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short indoor and outdoor stop on the Baie-des-Chaleurs side that breaks up the drive and suits younger children. Access needs were not answered, and hours and season were not checked.
